chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is disliked for a man to combine between the two sevens and the two circumambulations in the obligatory [prayer], but as for the optional [prayer], there is no problem.'

key_terms.الطَّوَافَيْنِ: The two circumambulations (referring to the two circuits of Tawaf al-Kitabah)
key_terms.الْأُسْبُوعَيْنِ: The two sevens (referring to the two cycles of the four-cycle prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to combine the two cycles of prayer during Tawaf al-Kitabah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between obligatory and voluntary prayers during Tawaf, ruling that combining the two cycles of the four-cycle prayer is merely disliked (makruh) in the former but fully permissible in the latter. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on facilitating worship in the sacred precincts of Mecca, distinguishing between the strict requirements of fard prayers and the flexibility granted to nafl acts. It underscores the principle that voluntary acts of worship allow for greater ease and combination to accommodate the physical demands of circumambulation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad in Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Zurara who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘But rather, it is disliked if the man were to gather between the two sevens and the two Tawaafs regarding the Obligatory. But, as for the optional, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘ Abd Allah ibn Muskan from Zurarah who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is Makruh (detestable) to perform two Tawaf of obligatory nature together; but in the case of optional Tawaf it is not harmful.’ ”
